title: Biomaterial track: Timoshenko hygromorph bilayer curvature and the 3/2 ceiling
converted_by: tracks/suite/make-cases.mjs; numbers are the agent's own, times are file times, see the header of that script

statement.text: Law: kappa = f(m,n) * delta_eps / h with f(m,n) = 6(1+m)^2 / [3(1+m)^2 + (1+mn)(m^2 + 1/(mn))], where m is the thickness ratio, n the modulus ratio, h the total thickness and delta_eps the differential free strain. Ceiling: kappa*h/delta_eps <= 3/2 for all positive m, n. The ceiling is proved in tracks/lean/HygromorphCeilingCheck.lean (timoshenkoCoefficient_le); tracks/research/lean/bm-lean-materials-laws__TimoshenkoCeilingUnique.lean adds that it is reached only at m^2 n = 1. items.what: The law as used: the 3/2 ceiling holds only if delta_eps is the true uniform differential strain and the sample is a narrow strip. In Rueggeberg's cyclic data delta_eps is inferred from bulk moisture change times a coefficient measured in a separate step test, and the strips are 20 mm wide at 4-6 mm thick. Under those inputs 9 of 12 records sit above 3/2, up to 2.06. Either the inferred strain is too small, or the strip assumption fails, or both; this run cannot separate them.
Earlier agent work (bm-wood-cellulose-hygromorphs.json) repeated the paper's '+11%, +13%, under 5%' cyclic error without recomputing from Table

Recomputed here, the excess is 7-66% and the dimensionless curvature breaks the ceiling. That file did note 1.53 in the ETH beech data and called it within uncertainty, which matches my held-out result.

Earlier work treated the ceiling as a design rule (delta_eps >= (2/3) kappa h) for sizing new materials. For thick wood under cycling, the bulk-moisture strain estimate under-predicts curvature by up to 66%, so that rule gives a strain floor that such data would appear to violate.

Data: most target papers could not be used. Reyssat & Mahadevan 2009, Holstov 2015, Correa 2015 and 2020, Gladman 2016 and the Le Duigou flax paper gave no open machine-readable text. Le Duigou & Castro 2016 reports force, not curvature. No classical bimetal measurements and no hydrogel bilayer with full inputs were found. The ETH dataset DOI returned HTTP
